title: Federal University Dutsin‑Ma Calls on Government to Fix Security, Facilities and Staffing Gaps
excerpt: The university’s VC urges the federal government to boost security, utilities and infrastructure as student numbers surge.
body:
The Federal University Dutsin‑Ma in Katsina State used its 10th and 11th combined convocation ceremonies to launch a public plea for federal assistance. Vice‑Chancellor Prof. Mohammed Othman warned that the institution is feeling the strain of rising enrolment, inadequate utilities and a shortage of teaching and support staff. He said the university’s take‑off campus is struggling to keep pace with expanding academic activities, and that the move to the permanent campus will only succeed with substantial government backing.

## Infrastructure and utilities need a boost

Prof. Othman listed a laundry list of missing essentials: reliable electricity and water supply, paved internal roads, enough lecture halls, modern laboratories, staff offices and student hostels. While the university has adopted a phased plan to shift academic and administrative functions to its permanent site, the lack of basic services is slowing progress. The VC emphasized that without federal funding for these core facilities, the quality of education could suffer.

## Security is a top priority

Security, especially in northern Nigeria, was highlighted as a non‑negotiable factor for the university’s mission. Othman described safety as “fundamental to the university’s ability to discharge its mandate.” He recounted a security retreat held in December 2025, which brought together security experts and agency representatives to audit existing measures and propose stronger surveillance, emergency response and inter‑agency coordination. Ongoing talks with the federal and state governments aim to fortify campus protection and reassure students and staff.

## Academic standards and staffing challenges

Despite the hurdles, the university reported encouraging academic outcomes. Nineteen of the thirty‑one programmes reviewed for the 2025/2026 session earned full five‑year accreditation from the National Universities Commission, while twelve received two‑year interim status. Four health‑related programmes have already secured professional accreditation, with results pending for others. However, Othman noted that staffing shortages, rising operational costs and limited funding continue to hamper progress. The university is pursuing staff promotions, addressing administrative backlogs and exploring alternative financing to bridge the gap.

The appeal, reported by Punch, underscores a broader call for coordinated investment in Nigeria’s higher‑education sector, particularly in regions facing security concerns. As Federal University Dutsin‑Ma works to expand its permanent campus and improve learning conditions, the hope is that federal intervention will turn these challenges into opportunities for growth.

## Looking ahead

The university’s leadership remains optimistic that with the right support, the permanent campus will soon become a hub of modern teaching, research and community engagement. Until then, the institution will continue to lobby for the resources needed to protect its students, staff and academic reputation.
